sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the festival of the Fifteenth of Av could be greater than the Torah-ordained festivals of Pesach, Sukkos, and Shavuos, and also greater than Yom Kippur, despite being instituted later.

translations.translation: But still, one must understand:
Behold, the festivals of Pesach and Sukkos
(and of Shavuos)
are from the Torah,
so how is it possible that the festival of the Fifteenth of Av should be greater than the festival of the Three Pilgrim Festivals?
Also, one must understand:
From the fact that it says, "There were no better festivals for Israel than the Fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur,"
and it places the Fifteenth of Av before Yom Kippur
[even though the festival of the Fifteenth of Av was instituted
(according to all the reasons in the Gemara)
several years after the festival of Yom Kippur],
it implies
that the festival of the Fifteenth of Av is also more elevated than the festival of Yom Kippur,
and this requires explanation:
Behold, even on Yom Kippur there is an ascent from an undesirable state,
so what is the superiority of the Fifteenth of Av over Yom Kippur?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between the general world (called "land") and the Garden of Eden (called "field"), based on their respective sources in Malchus—the external speech of Malchus versus its internal three upper sefiros.

translations.translation: And this will be understood based on what is explained in the maamar, "The explanation of the verse,"18
"The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field."19
For "land" refers to the entirety of the world,
and "field"
(the choicest part of the land)
is the Garden of Eden.
And this distinction between the entirety of the world and the Garden of Eden
(that the entirety of the world is called "land" and the Garden of Eden is called "field")
is in their source.
For the coming into being of the world is from the aspect of speech of Malchus
(the externality of Malchus20)
which is called "land,"
and the Garden of Eden is from the aspect of the first three [sefiros] of Malchus
(the inwardness of Malchus20)
which is called "field,"
as explained in the maamar.
For the speech of Malchus
(the ten utterances with which the world was created21)
its function is to bring created beings into existence,
analogous to speech in a person, which is for the sake of another,
and the first three [sefiros] of Malchus are the inwardness of Malchus, which receives from Yesod,
which is22
the conclusion of Atzilus
(the end of the body23),
analogous to the emotions in a person,
for although they relate to another,
nevertheless their function is24
that the person is aroused and affected.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Garden of Eden has an additional advantage: the flow there comes from the intellect (mochin) via Yesod, and through the work in the field, the flow of the Kesser (supreme King) above the chain of descent is drawn down.

translations.translation: And the maamar adds that there is yet another advantage of the Garden of Eden over the entirety of the world:
The flow into the world is from the emotions,
for the speech of Malchus receives from the emotions,25
and the flow into the Garden of Eden is from the intellect,
and as explained there,
that which Yesod is called by the name "Kol" (all)26
is because of the fifty gates of Binah that are drawn into it
(Kol in gematria is fifty27),
therefore,
since the Garden of Eden is from the inwardness of Malchus, which receives from Yesod,
behold, through Yesod, the intellect is also drawn into the Garden of Eden.
And this is "The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field,"
that the advantage of the land
(the entirety of the world,
whose coming into being is from the speech of Malchus)
is "in everything" (bakol),
the drawing of Yesod,
and through this – the drawing of the intellect,
and then the revelation of Elokus is drawn also into the entirety of the world,
as in the Garden of Eden.
And "a king for a cultivated field" is as stated in the Zohar,28
"Who is the King? That is the Supreme King who joins with the field when it is cultivated,"
that through the service in the Garden of Eden
(a cultivated field)
the drawing of the Kesser
(the Supreme King)
which is above the chain of descent, is effected.
